condition.notes: Rail resistance to ground is low (under 10 ohm), suggesting a possible short. This is a SUSPECT, not a confirmed short — low resistance can also be a normal low-impedance rail (e.g. a CPU VCORE rail reads low ohms to ground by design). The technician must confirm with a thermal scan or current-limited injection. Do NOT treat as a confirmed short without confirmation.

next_steps.action: Rail resistance to ground is LOW (<10 ohm). This MIGHT be a short, or it might be normal for a low-impedance rail. Confirm with a current-limited supply (inject the rail's nominal voltage at ~0.5A limit) and thermal imaging. A genuinely shorted component will heat visibly; a healthy low-impedance rail will not.

measure.what: Confirm short via current-limited injection + thermal
measure.where: Rail test point, with current-limited bench supply
measure.instrument: Current-limited bench supply + thermal camera (or freeze spray)
measure.expected: A shorted component heats visibly under injection. No thermal signature = healthy low-impedance rail.
measure.safety: Use a current-limited supply, NOT the on-board regulator. Limit to ~0.5A to avoid trace damage.

interpretations.then: That component is shorted. Replace it. After replacement, re-measure resistance to confirm it returned to normal.
The low resistance is normal for this rail (low-impedance design). The fault is NOT a short. Re-examine other causes.
